L0@P0: STUDY TITLE: “Improving GI function in cancer patients:
L1@P0: the potential of metoclopramide to decrease vincristineinduced GI ileus”
L2@P0: Lymphoma is a common cancer in dogs, and the current standard
L3@P0: of chemotherapy is the multi-agent CHOP protocol. This treatment
L4@P0: involves a drug called vincristine, which can induce gastrointestinal
L5@P0: (GI) ileus in the canine patient. This health issue can lead to nausea,
L6@P0: decreased appetite and stomach upset.
L7@P0: This WCVM clinical trial's goal is to determine if metoclopramide,
L8@P0: a drug that's commonly used to treat and prevent nausea, can
L9@P0: alleviate the GI ileus due to vincristine.
L10@P0: Q. What do study participants receive?
L11@P0: All dogs enrolled in the clinical trial receive:
L12@P0: • complimentary flow cytometry
L13@P0: • MDR-1 testing (multi-drug sensitivity)
L14@P0: • abdominal ultrasound examination
L15@P0: Q. What dogs are eligible?
L16@P0: The research team is seeking dogs (all breeds and sizes) that have
L17@P0: been diagnosed with multicentric lymphoma (substage a) and are
L18@P0: pursuing the CHOP chemotherapy treatment protocol at the WCVM
L19@P0: Veterinary Medical Centre.
L20@P0: Questions?
L21@P0: Please contact Dr. Arata Matsuyama (medical.oncology@usask.ca)
L22@P0: for more details.

L24@P0: Veterinary medical oncology
L25@P0: Clinical trial opportunity
L26@P0: For dogs diagnosed with canine
L27@P0: lymphoma and receiving chemotherapy

L64: # Current Oncology Clinical Trials
L65: 
L66: Although we are making considerable progress in the fight against cancer, we still have a long way to go. Often, the best new information about cancer comes from animals participating in a clinical trial.
L67: 
L68: If you do not live in our region of the country, you could check with the 【57†Veterinary Cancer Society†www.vetcancersociety.org】  to learn about clinical trials in your area.
L69: 
L70: * * *
L71: ## Emerging Canine Cancer Studies
L72: 
L73: We are currently recruiting for Emerging Canine Cancer Studies
L74: 
L75:   * High Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) for Lymphoma in Dogs
L76:   * High Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) for Osteosarcoma in Dogs
L77:   * Immunotherapy Trial of New Cancer Vaccine
L78: 
L79: 【58†Learn more about our Emerging Canine Cancer Studies】
L80: 
L81: * * *
L82: ## Canine Urinary Bladder Cancer
L83: 
L84: For dogs with urinary bladder cancer (TCC) affecting the bladder and/or urethra. The study is aimed at learning how the dog’s immune system can be stimulated to attack the cancer.
L85: 
L86: 【59†Learn more about our Canine Urinary Bladder Cancer Trial】
L87: 
L88: * * *
L89: ## Canine Osteosarcoma
L90: 
L91: The WCORC and Purdue Institute for Cancer Research have recently launched a research program in canine osteosarcoma to identify new, effective therapies in dogs that will improve cure rates for both dogs and humans with this cancer.
L92: Our current focus is on collecting tumor tissues from dogs undergoing amputation to analyze them for susceptibility to novel drugs. A financial incentive of $500 per dog is available to help offset the cost of amputation to the owners of dogs contributing to this research.
L93: We are excited to announce a new clinical trial for osteosarcoma that studies the clinical, molecular, and immune characterization of this tumor type. Eligible dogs must have a confirmed diagnosis, no evidence of metastasis, or spread, to other parts of the body, and received no prior treatment.
L94: 
L95: 【60†Learn more about our Clinical, Molecular, and Immune Characterization of Naturally-Occurring Osteosarcoma Clinical Trial】
L96: 
L97: * * *
L98: ## Tumor Ablation Studies
L99: 
L100: H-FIRE Liver Cancer Study is evaluating the safety and immune effects of High-Frequency Irreversible Electroporation (H-FIRE) for dogs diagnosed with liver cancer.
L101: The goals of this study are to evaluate the safety and feasibility of H-FIRE in dogs with liver cancer, measure local and systemic immune responses after H-FIRE treatment, analyze tumor biopsies, blood immune cells, and cytokines before and after treatment, and determine whether a single H-FIRE treatment can stimulate a meaningful anti-tumor immune response.
L102: 
L103: 【61†Learn more about our H-FIRE Liver Cancer Study】
L104: 
L105: * * *
L106: ## Emerging Immunotherapy Study
L107: 
L108: Purdue is evaluating new immunotherapy approaches designed to help a dog's own immune system better recognize and fight cancer.  Currently, studies include evaluating MO29, a new drug that blocks SHP-1, a protein that can limit the immune system's response to cancer.
L109: 
L110: 【62†Learn more about SHP-1 inhibitor study】

L26: Clinical trials
L27: How can I find an ongoing clinical trial?
L28: 
L29: Via the search button, you can perform a targeted search for canine clinical trials. In order to do this, tick -if known- the box of your dog’s tumour type (‘Select tumour type’) and/or the countries (‘Select location’) for which you wish to know whether clinical trials are ongoing.
L30: 
L31: Afterwards, a list of trials for which your dog might be eligible will appear. The listed information is limited to
L32:   * Treatment centre where the trial is available
L33:   * In/exclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria describe the criteria necessary for your dog to participate in the trial (e.g. inoperable tumour). Exclusion criteria describe conditions that exclude possible participation to the trial (e.g. concomitant chemotherapy).
L34:   * Contact information: phone number and e-mail address of the trial’s contact person, webpage with more information on the trial.
L35: For more details on the trial, we recommend you to contact the researchers via the listed contact info.
